title: A merge that changes the page code republishes the page
why:
The Cockpit ran main's page code from before batch 122 until triage republished it at 09:43 CST Nov 13 (owner asked 09:39 CST). Two done steps were meant to stop this. c130's republish is a prose step for the batch runner, and batch 122 skipped it. page-stale-hook reads a stamp at <git common dir>/waiting-page-built (stale_pages.py read_stamp) and stays silent with no stamp, so in a fresh cloud container it likely never fires (retrospective's code reading, not probed). The Status tab also lags: nothing republishes it after each batch.

Lane started 00:24 CST Nov 15 (coordinator 00:25 CST, relayed): lane session_013NEJL2czk9NMmNAAjzVujL, "a merge that changes the page code republishes the page". It read running and parented to the coordinator in list_sessions; its task summary read "git checkout -b page-republish-at-merge origin/main".

Triage's republish duty (skill waiting-page, republish steps): once the lane's reader lands, each republish by triage also writes page-built.json. source: retrospective 09:43 CST Nov 13, answering the owner's 09:39 CST question
note: (a) merge --confirm on a batch whose diff touches skills/waiting-page/page.html prints the republish as a post-merge act, and the runner's report carries 'republished: <pages>' or a reason. (b) The stamp moves from the local git dir to the record branch, so a cloud session reads it. (c) Until step page-data-one-store lands, triage republishes the Status tab at each batch review (triage does this from batch 131 on, as a stood pick; undo: drop it from the batch review). Done when a test merge that touches page.html, from a fresh cloud container, gets a 'behind' line or a refusal. Probe first: confirm the no-stamp silence in a cloud container.
